summary: Yu-min Lee works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Lee studied under graduate supervisor John C. Huntington until around 1983 and later served as a Professor at National Taiwan University.
Yuan Ren is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. Ren completed a PhD at McMaster University in 1998, studying under doctoral supervisor Phyllis Granoff and committee member Koichi Shinohara.

Yuanxing Guo (1920–1982) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Gangkar Rinpoche around 1946. He held a post as a researcher at the Chinese Buddhist Culture Research Institute and worked at the Jinling Sutra Publishing House.

Yudru Tsomu is a scholar in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She earned a PhD from Harvard University around 2006 under Leonard van der Kuijp, with advisors Mark C. Elliott, Janet Gyatso, and Philip A. Kuhn, and teachers James E. Bosson and Wesley M. Jacobsen.
Yuexia (1858–1917) was a Buddhist studies figure who founded Huayan University, where he served as a teacher from around 1912 to 1916.

Yuguang Liu works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Liu studied at Northwest Minzu University in 2000 under Bsam gtan, Tashi Tsering, Gongbaojie, and Gyalog, and completed a PhD at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology in 2005.
Yuhiko Katsuzaki (1946–) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from around 1965 to 1975. He later served as president (学長) of Taisho University from around 2011 to 2013.

Yui Suzuki works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Suzuki studied at the University of California, Los Angeles until around 2005 under William M. Bodiford, Lothar von Falkenhausen, and Donald F. McCallum, and held a post at the University of Maryland, College Park around 2006.

Yuichi Kajiyama (1925–2004) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Kyoto University, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, SOAS, and the University of Vienna, he held faculty posts at Kyoto, Bukkyo, and Soka Universities.

Yuishin Ito (1931–2023) studied at Bukkyo and Doshisha universities. In Buddhist studies, he held posts at Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (~1961–1968), Bukkyo University (~1968–1997), Kyoto Bunkyo Gakuen, Shōjōke-in Temple (~2003–2009), and Chion-in Temple (~2010–2020).

Yujun Endo (1939–2021) specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He held appointments as an Associate Professor at Taisho University and as an advisor (相談役) at the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Yuka Otani is a scholar in Buddhist studies who has held posts as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at Ryukoku University and Hanazono University.

Yukei Matsunaga (1929–2023) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Tohoku University and earned a doctorate from Kyushu University in 1978, later serving as Director at Koyasan University (~1968–1980) and holding a post at Shuchiin University.
Yuki Takatsukasa is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University and served there as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師).

Yukihiko Asayama works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He served as a researcher overseas (文部省在外研究員) at South China Normal University from around 1996 to 1997 and held a professorship (教授) at Hokkaido University of Education.

Yukihiro Okada specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1976–1981) and under Michael Hahn (~1981–1984), and served as an assistant professor (助教授) at Kobe Women's University Seto Junior College around 1989.

Yukio Sakamoto (1899–1973) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1920–1926) under Taiken Kimura and Daito Shimaji. He held posts at Toyo University and served as President of Rissho University (~1968–1971).
Yukio Yamanaka is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He completed graduate studies at Kyoto University and served as a DFG Research Fellow at the University of Göttingen.
Yuko Kamishima (1971–) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Tokyo, was a research student under Ekai Kawaguchi, and held a post at Ritsumeikan University.
Yuko Matsuda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Aoyama Gakuin Women's Junior College and held a post at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College.
